75: MISHNA. Can be acquired through money or through a document - the Gemara will derive the source.
Through years - he goes free after six years.
Or through the Jubilee - if the Jubilee year is encountered during the [standard] six[-year term].

Or through the deduction of money - he can redeem himself; his master deducts the cost of his labor for the years that have already passed from the cost of his redemption, all according a calculation based on his purchase price. As it is written: "The price of sale shall be applied to the number of years" (Leviticus 25:50) -- if he bought him for six Maneh, and he is due to go [free] after six [years], it turns out that he acquires the labor of each year for one Maneh.

More than him - since she acquires herself with all these modes, as well as through signs indicating puberty, as we derived earlier (Kiddushin 4a:3) from "Then shall she go out for nothing." (Exodus 21:11)

Or through the death of the master - and he does not serve [the master's] heirs. But as for a slave who is sold for his initial period, whose master dies within the six[-year term, the slave must] complete [the term] for his heirs. All this is derived in the Gemara.
